messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: runtime-agent detected repeated CUDA illegal-memory-access on gw-infr-08 (container: runtime-worker-7). Spike started ~2635000100, rate ~3/min. Auto-cordon initiated.

alex: seeing the same in prod-routes, several containers hitting SIGSEGV during model load. stack shows device pointer translation failure.

maria: confirming nvml logs from gw-infr-08 attached to the incident. GPU 1 reports address fault, `cuCtxSynchronize` failing.

alex: rolling the node out of rotation now — `kubectl cordon gw-infr-08 && kubectl drain gw-infr-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to clear inflight. customers with heavy streaming traffic may see 5xx while routes rehome.

jen: flagged customer success for possible blips: pinging enterprise accounts on dedicated capacity now. ETA 10m for rehoming. @maria please confirm which customers were routed to that node.

maria: customers A and C had flows on that zone, both on dedicated pools. Raising severity to P2 due to potential tail-latency impact.

alex: quick mitigation plan: 1) cordon/drain node (in-progress), 2) disable fast-kv-cache on affected model variant to avoid heavy device-side allocation, 3) fallback to quantized-CPU variant for low-priority routes, 4) collect coredumps + nvcrash logs and upload to shared bucket, 5) notify kernel team if misalignment reproduces.

ops-bot: Action: cordon/drain started by alex at 2635000140.

maria: dumping dmesg from the host: ````
[ 3456.789012] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Ch 00000004, engine 00000001, reason: MMU fault: FAULT at 0x7f8c12345000, read
[ 3456.789015] NVRM: GPU memory access at address 0x7f8c12345000 caused illegal access
````
This looks like misaligned device pointer — not classic OOM.

jen: how reproducible is this? any correlation with our new allocator patch we rolled last week?

alex: good call — we shipped the patched slab allocator (fast-alloc v2) in the canary pool 48h ago. I'm going to flip the allocator flag off for canary and affected pools: `REDWOOD_FLAGS=fast_alloc_v2=false` and redeploy.

maria: note: we have a hotfix path: rollback allocator flag + restart runtime containers on gw-infr-*. That should reduce illegal-access frequency if it's an allocator-induced misalignment.

ops-bot: Redeploy initiated by alex at 2635000235: flow: set flag -> rolling restart runtime pods on node pool.

km_team: (kernel-maintainer) seeing the dmesg trace now. If the GPU MMU hits a misaligned pointer the driver will raise Xid 31. Need full coredump + userspace backtrace to be sure; please save `/var/crash/*` and `nvidia-smi --query` outputs. We'll triage once uploaded.

alex: logs and coredump uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/2635000123/ — added nvml logs, runtime stdout, and heap profiles.

maria: initial customer impact summary: 2 enterprise flows saw 10-30s error bursts during rehome; one short fallback to CPU variant reduced throughput but kept requests alive. No long-term data loss. CS notified.

jen: deploying temporary routing tweak: mark low-priority routes to `cpu-quant` model variant to reduce GPU allocation pressure across the pool. Will revert after node stabilization.

alex: still seeing occasional illegal-access on gw-infr-09 after allocator flip. That node has older kernel 5.15. Suspect race between allocator and kernel page-table handling. Escalating to kernel & infra: @km_team can you correlate kernel versions?

km_team: confirmed gw-infr-09 is 5.15.42 while canary nodes are 6.1. We'll reproduce on 5.15 in lab. If it's a kernel-driver interaction, we may need a driver patch or revert our allocator.

maria: ops-bot triggered mitigation: autoscaler set to prefer nodes with kernel >=6.0 for the next hour. Also set dedicated pools to prefer hostnames gw-infr-1..6.

ops-bot: Policy applied at 2635000380.

jen: customer update: emailed affected customers with brief summary, ETA for full root-cause 24-48h. Support ticket R-8673 created.

alex: next steps: continue draining older-kernel nodes, keep allocator disabled in production pools until post-mortem, collect more reproducible traces in lab, coordinate kernel/driver patch if needed. I'll post follow-up when lab repro is confirmed.

maria: added short runbook notes to incident doc: if Xid 31 recurs, cordon node, toggle `fast_alloc_v2` off, restart runtime pods, escalate to kernel team.

ops-bot: Incident status: containment in progress, customer impact limited, oncall handoff scheduled to maria at 2635000400.

maria: taking over for the night. leaving notes here. if anyone finds a deterministic reproducer please upload to the incident bucket and ping me. :thumbsup:
